data.title: Nvidia approached Arm CEO Haas to succeed Huang, FT reports
data.description: Nov 13 : Nvidia's board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Haas is among several candidates being considered to succeed Huang and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, FT reported. The British chipmaker declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report. Arm's US-listed shared pared losses after the report and were down more than 5 per cent. Nvidia's shares were down over 3 per cent.

data.title: German watchdog warns some cooling systems remain vulnerable to hacking
data.description: BERLIN, Nov 13 : Germany's information security office BSI warned on Friday of ongoing vulnerabilities in some of Danish firm Danfoss' industrial cooling appliances, following cyberattacks on refrigeration systems across Europe. The systems in question should be taken offline when possible or otherwise any connection should be secured via VPN, or Virtual Private Network, BSI said in a security advisory on its website. Hacking attacks on European supermarkets spread across the continent last week, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month. At least some of the refrigerator units affected used temperature control technology from Danfoss that was also targeted in the French ​attack.  The German office said IT security managers should also check whether they can install updates available from the company. It warned, however, that Danfoss had not yet provided sufficient software updates to counter the attacks. "Even new patches do not guarantee that further vulnerabilities in an affected product will not come to light in the near future. Industrial control systems should therefore not be directly accessible from the internet."   The United States last week also warned of a "cyber threat" to industrial refrigeration systems.

data.title: Neoclouds, AI stocks slide again as Nvidia turmoil rattles sector
data.description: Nov 13 : Shares of AI-related US companies dropped again on Friday, with neoclouds among the worst hit, fueled by fresh jitters over AI financing following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 declined 2.2 per cent, on pace to erase almost $870 billion in market value if the losses hold through the close. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index also shed 6 per cent, facing a more than $670 billion wipeout for the day. CoreWeave and Nebius Group, neocloud firms backed by Nvidia, slumped 10.8 per cent and 12.1 per cent, respectively, extending their sharp declines from Thursday when longtime CEO Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs. Nvidia, under Huang, has financed infrastructure built around its chips, a strategy that has driven demand but also raised questions about circular funding flows between the chipmaker and its customers. "It's a short-term death blow to the industry because the amount of vendor financing and financing guarantees that Nvidia and Jensen Huang stepped into are now over," said Thomas Hayes, chairman of Great Hill Capital LLC. Further, Nscale, a British cloud provider also backed by Nvidia, amended its IPO filing to say it expects to report a net loss of $1.7 billion in the nine months ended September 30, wider than the $433.3 million net loss a year ago. Chip stocks, widely regarded as among the biggest winners of the AI boom, also dropped. Advanced Micro Devices fell 10.2 per cent and Broadcom lost 6.7 per cent after both gained for the last five sessions. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology shed 5.6 per cent while data storage companies Western Digital and Sandisk dipped 7.7 per cent and 9.3 per cent, respectively. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent, along with AI server makers Dell and HPE, fell between 6.2 per cent and 10.7 per cent each. Utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the AI boom, including GE Vernova, Constellation Energy and Vistra, eased about 2 per cent to 3.3 per cent each. AI hyperscalers were also mostly lower, barring Meta Platforms, which rose 1.3 per cent. Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft fell between 0.1 per cent and 3.6 per cent. Nvidia's quarterly earnings and AI lab Anthropic's much-awaited public markets debut are set for next week and could prove to be catalysts for sentiment towards AI. "You have no idea what to expect from Nvidia. That's the problem. This company is pure uncertainty right now," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

data.title: Dollar set for biggest weekly gain in two months
data.description: NEW YORK/GDANSK, Nov 13 : The dollar was on track for its strongest weekly rise in two months on Friday, holding near a 19-month high as rising bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike lifted US Treasury yields, while the yen hovered around 160 per dollar and kept traders alert for possible intervention from Tokyo. Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and this week's stronger-than-expected US inflation data have left traders weighing the prospect of a larger-than-usual Fed rate hike next month. Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 32 basis points so far this week to around 4.84 per cent, on course for their biggest weekly jump since April 2025. The euro was down 0.23 per cent at $1.103, after hitting its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was on course for its fourth straight week of losses. The dollar was up 0.28 per cent to 0.837 against the Swiss franc and was set to snap two straight weeks of losses.  "The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller." Traders are pricing in a roughly 92 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.  The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was up 0.1 per cent at 103.34, clinging to its highest since April 2025 and on track for its biggest weekly gain since September. That would be its third straight week of gains. YEN FOCUS           The yen was steady at 159.84 per dollar, around its weakest since early September, fuelling concerns about possible intervention. The currency has weakened about 1 per cent this week, on track for its biggest weekly loss since September.  Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility. The Australian dollar was down 0.46 per cent at $0.678. The Aussie is the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is the only G10 country for which markets are pricing a rate cut next year. [AUD/]  The New Zealand kiwi weakened 0.29 per cent versus the greenback to $0.553 and was on course for its third straight week of losses. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.73 per cent to $68,126.21. Ethereum declined 5.02 per cent to $1,914.61.

data.title: Fed's Warsh to take stock of AI revolution as US public grows wary
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 13 : Federal Reserve officials expect artificial intelligence will reshape the US economy, an idea that proponents of the technology in Silicon Valley have plastered on billboards and TV and pushed in public debate as they channel trillions of dollars into data centers and billions into their bank accounts. But how the region's new tech boom evolves, and on what timetable, remains a wild card for central bankers responsible for managing inflation and employment in the short term. In a public forum on Monday in San Francisco, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will try to understand better the risks and benefits he and his colleagues may have to balance — from the possible large-scale loss of jobs to the promise of rapid economic growth and falling prices. The forum, the only scheduled public event of the five task forces Warsh established early in his tenure this year to review issues of major importance to the Fed, will take him to the epicenter of an emerging industry he sees as a "hinge point in history," even as last week's midterm elections sparked a backlash against rapid data center construction and raised the specter of deepening inequality. For all of AI's disinflationary potential, Warsh is convening the discussion while the frenetic AI buildout is having the opposite effect — driving up prices in a way that increasingly concerns many Fed officials, with no clarity for when it may let up and with the possibility the central bank may need to slow the very thing Warsh sees as revolutionary. More broadly, what seemed a clear proposition of supercharged growth and buoyant productivity when Warsh spoke while auditioning for the Fed job — he was also an investor in AI firms but sold his holdings under Fed ethics rules — is now at the center of a national debate that could change the industry's trajectory. Though driven by local politics, the concerns range from local land use to the impact on children's and societal mental health, the potential for stress in financial markets as capital is channeled through increasingly complex AI funding vehicles, and, most recently, risks to national security after revelations about a top tech industry executive's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. "We have to make sure that AI is used responsibly and ethically," Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee said recently as she joined a movement to ban local data center construction that has taken root just across San Francisco Bay. "It can't become a tool that compounds the biases that are already built into our systems. It can't be a tool for harm, for discrimination, or for displacement." EVOLVING VIEWS It may be difficult for participants in the three-hour forum on Monday to cover the sweeping set of issues that will determine whether AI deployment accelerates or slows, and therefore how deep an impact it might have on inflation, employment and other data the Fed watches. An agenda published by the San Francisco Fed says the event, including three panels of speakers bookended by comments from Warsh, will offer "input from a wide range of stakeholders on technology's implications for the economy and the labor market." It will be a homecoming of sorts for the Fed chief. He attended nearby Stanford University with some of the tech industry's leading figures and appointed one of them, Marc Andreessen, to chair the task force that will focus on AI, which Warsh has come to call "super intelligence" in line with President Donald Trump's wishes. Other members of the productivity and jobs task force include Chad Jones, a Stanford University economics professor now working with the internal think tank of AI firm Anthropic, which is on the verge of an initial public offering that would value the company at more than $1 trillion, and Asha Sharma, who runs Microsoft's Xbox business. Fed officials began focusing on AI even before Warsh took the helm, with the pace of research and discussion accelerating after the release of the ChatGPT generative AI chatbot in 2022 and the start of breathtaking changes for a technology that a decade ago had trouble telling a cat from a kitchen table. Thanks to breakthroughs in large language models and the massive assemblage of computing power, AI is now solving advanced math and medical problems, turning novice entrepreneurs into software engineers, and offering bespoke "agentic" services that can do legal or scientific research or take over personal bill-paying and daily planning. While Warsh initially saw AI as providing a downdraft on inflation through higher productivity — a free ride of sorts that could allow central bankers to keep interest rates lower than would otherwise be expected — he has taken a more nuanced view since arriving at the Fed in May. The shift reflects the uncertain timetable for productivity benefits, the potentially inflationary investment needed to realize them, and views about job-market impacts that range from a lift-all-boats boost to a Dickensian world of chronic underemployment. 'TRULY HISTORIC' INVESTMENT At a forum in Oakland in September, where the city's mayor issued her warning about AI, Fed Governor Lisa Cook, whose academic research focused on innovation, reiterated concerns that AI would lead to "at least a temporary increase in the unemployment rate" and possibly a jump in the underlying level of joblessness. Fed Governor Michael Barr raised similar concerns on Thursday, saying the US should prepare for "serious short-term disruptions" to the job market depending on how fast AI is deployed and whether it remains broadly available and affordable to businesses regardless of size. For the moment, though, AI investments are propping up US growth, stock-market gains, and consumer and business spending that might otherwise be unremarkable. "You have this investment that is truly historic. You are talking railroad-plus-interstate-highways-historic," Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said recently at a chamber of commerce event in South Carolina where attendees pumped him for insight on what the AI boom might mean. "If that historic investment does not pay off and people scale back, you worry what is going to happen." Although all the members of the task force Warsh picked are from the tech world, neither they nor the Fed chief will have the last word on how any recommendations find their way into Fed policy. That matter will be left to officials like Barkin, who said he hoped the discussion on Monday would cover the full landscape of issues. "I'm hopeful we'll hear the strongest possible evangelist's view, as well as the strongest possible other view," Barkin said. "Then we'll have a chance to wrestle with it."

data.title: Uber says US drivers' license data stolen in data breach
data.description: Nov 13 : Uber said an unauthorized party used compromised credentials at a service provider to access its data, according to a notice posted on the California attorney general's website. The notice, dated November 10, said the provider told Uber on October 9 that the credentials had been compromised and used to access Uber's account with the provider. Uber severed its data connections with the provider and opened an investigation. On October 13, the investigation determined the party had used the credentials to access Uber data, and that the recipients' personal information was among the data accessed, the notice said.  The notice did not name the provider or list the data involved. TechCrunch reported on Friday that the provider was Fireworks AI and that the data included drivers' license information.  Uber and Fireworks AI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The notice said the incident affected about 1,873 Rhode Island residents. It also carried instructions for residents of the District of Columbia, Maryland, North Carolina, New York and Pennsylvania. Uber said it is offering affected people free credit monitoring and fraud assistance through Cyberscout, a TransUnion company. Recipients have 90 days from the date of the letter to enroll. The company said it had not identified any misuse of the data to date.

data.title: Exclusive-Amazon’s plan to own the world’s product data and fight AI shopping agents
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 13 : Amazon has a secret plan to ensure shoppers never need to leave its site: own the world’s product information.   Called World Product Graph, the initiative seeks to hoover up data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not, according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, and to people familiar with the matter. In so doing, Amazon could truly become the everything store, offering deep data on a vast array of goods and cutting in to Google's dominance in online search, while also fending off rival Walmart's growing e-commerce business. It also serves to address the continued rise of AI agents, software that can complete shopping tasks autonomously for users. According to the document, Amazon's own AI-driven search agent often provides inaccurate information. And if fully implemented, World Product Graph could draw shoppers away from rival e-commerce sites that have far less data.  “Amazon cannot be the go-destination for every shopping mission if customers must leave to research product relationships on Google, brand websites, and review sites,” according to the document. “These answers exist, but the only way to find them has been to leave Amazon for painstaking research on brand websites, third party review sites and tech forums.” Reuters could not determine if or when this plan may be implemented, though the document, written like a press release, has an aspirational future release date of October 1, 2027. "Draft, outdated documents often paint an incomplete picture and the existence of a brainstorming document such as this one doesn't necessarily reflect our current plans," said Amazon, in a statement. "We're constantly working on new ideas and technologies to make Amazon's product catalog comprehensive, accurate, and helpful for customers." Already, many consumers begin researching products on Amazon. But according to a 2025 Morgan Stanley research report, the 16 per cent of online shoppers who do so on Amazon is dwarfed by Google’s 57 per cent. However, when customers know exactly what product they plan to buy, Amazon has the advantage, with 41 per cent of searches starting there, compared with 23 per cent for Google and 18 per cent for Walmart. 'THE EVERYTHING STORE' World Product Graph “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” the document says. That will entail some brands and retailers contributing product data continuously to Amazon, but also Amazon independently crawling other retailers’ websites.   Reuters could not determine how Amazon planned to crawl the sites or whether it would need to seek permission in all cases. Amazon has already signed up Coca-Cola and Bayer, among others, to contribute product data, the document says. And the company held a “CEO-level P&G/Amazon summit” for a trial with Procter & Gamble. The companies didn't respond to requests for comment. Amazon is shuffling staff internally to get the project off the ground, according to one of the people, though Reuters could not determine if the October 1 date is a realistic deadline for making the plan public.  The document laying out the plan is what is known internally as a PR/FAQ — press release and frequently asked questions — which is typically a six-page narrative memo laying out the rationale and business case for a new product or service. Not all PR/FAQs lead to a service being introduced and, the people said, World Product Graph could be modified or aborted due to financial or other concerns.  The project is part of Amazon’s Selection & Catalog Systems unit, according to the document, and is being organized under Robert Tekiela, a vice president in the division. He did not respond to a request for comment. With the more complete data, Amazon can help users determine with more certainty which is the most recent model or colorway of a vacuum cleaner or tablet computer while also guiding them toward more subjective criteria like which is best for them based on their shopping history or other data, the document shows. The project would also address problems with Amazon’s own AI-powered search engine known as Rufus, which the company began calling “Alexa for Shopping” in May. “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete, but customers lack expertise to detect these errors,” the document says. Further, users conduct about 83 million searches weekly using Rufus, and running them is “expensive,” according to the document. More data would allow Amazon to use less expensive models, more efficiently. “I used to spend an hour on Reddit figuring this stuff out,” says a fake customer in an imagined quote in the document. “It’s like the store finally knows what it’s selling.”  In its statement to Reuters, Amazon, referring to the PR/FAQ, said, "the usage figures are significantly outdated" and that its data shows that Alexa for Shopping is roughly 97 per cent accurate globally. BATTLING AGENTS World Product Graph would help serve at least one other important function — staving off the growing threat of alternative AI shopping agents, the people said. CEO Andy Jassy sought during the company's third-quarter earnings call to downplay agents' impact, saying “few customers are doing much shopping this way yet” and that Amazon’s advertising business has been minimally impacted.    Yet Amazon executives have grown wary of AI shopping agents that may send customer traffic to other sites that have greater or more complete data, according to people familiar with the matter. Meta’s Muse agent, for instance, has proven popular with customers already, garnering more than 10 million users in the US and Canada since launching in September. Amazon in the same month blocked Muse from its retail site and last year sued AI firm Perplexity to prevent similar access, a case that is still ongoing.   Jassy said Alexa for Shopping has been used by over 400 million people in the past year. Muse, however, "has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT,” JPMorgan said in a research note. Responding to a post saying xAI's Grok agent was blocked on Amazon, Elon Musk wrote on X last month: “Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon."    By creating the world's most extensive storehouse of product data, Amazon could ensure AI agents working on behalf of shoppers will be compelled to seek products out on Amazon.com and not other retailers’ sites, the people said. That would also help protect Amazon’s growing advertising business. Employees have described World Product Graph as the beginnings of an effort to make the site a one-stop shop for buying anything imaginable, an expansion of existing services known as “Buy for Me” and “Shop Direct,” which list on Amazon products sold on other sites, allowing customers to buy them with Amazon as an intermediary. “Customers have always been able to find products on Amazon,” Tekiela said in the document. “What’s been missing is understanding – how do these products relate to each other, which one is right for me, and what else should I consider?”

data.title: SpaceX to attempt first Starship spacecraft recovery on land in 15th flight
data.description: BROWNSVILLE, Texas, Nov 13 : SpaceX's latest Starship flight planned for Friday will include its first attempt to catch the spacecraft at its Texas launch site rather than discarding it in the ocean, a key test of Elon Musk’s bid to make a fully reusable rocket system. The 407-foot-tall (124 m) Starship rocket is scheduled to launch at 4:45 p.m. CT (2245 GMT) from SpaceX's Starbase launch facilities in South Texas for its 15th flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for its satellite connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket still in development. SpaceX as of Friday morning had not received a launch license from the US Federal Aviation Administration. The FAA, which has typically issued licenses a day prior to past Starship launches, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Musk's space and AI colossus views the next-generation Starship rocket as crucial to expanding its Starlink network with more satellites and, in the future, deploying a vast swarm of AI data-processing satellites called Starmind, as the company increasingly positions itself as an infrastructure giant. SpaceX last launched Starship in September, taking the rocket and its satellites to orbit for the first time despite some engines shutting down mid-flight. That mission, planned to last 10 hours, ended after roughly 3 hours with an intact splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. For Friday's mission, the company expects to return to Texas both Starship's Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage it launches to space. The upper stage - the top half of the rocket that serves as the spacecraft - will return some 22 hours after launch. SpaceX has said it would be a "breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket" if all goes as planned. MAKING WAY FOR STARSHIP SpaceX has returned the 236-foot tall Super Heavy booster three times to its launchpad after sending Starship to space, falling back vertically into large mechanical arms fixed to its launch tower some 10 minutes after launch. The last such "tower catch" was in March 2025. For the 15th mission, SpaceX will need to move the Super Heavy booster off the launchpad to make way for Starship, which is expected to fall from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth. That sets up the debut Starship catch to occur around 2:45 p.m. CT (2045 GMT) on Saturday. Musk has said he expects to enter a weekly cadence of Starship launches by the first half of 2027, while SpaceX has said it could begin launching Starship from a new Florida launchpad by the end of 2026. NASA has helped fund Starship's development with roughly $3.2 billion delivered to SpaceX since selecting the rocket in 2021 to serve as a moon lander for its astronauts under the multibillion-dollar US Artemis moon program. SpaceX has put at least $15 billion of its own funds into the rocket's development. NASA and SpaceX expect Starship to land humans on the moon by 2028, though several major testing milestones remain that analysts and industry engineers believe will push that timeline back. Those milestones include demonstrating complex fuel transfers between Starship "tanker" rockets in orbit, a key process that will enable Starship to travel beyond Earth's orbit to the moon. Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin is also developing a moon lander, Blue Moon, for NASA under the Artemis program. Blue Moon is poised to join Starship and another spacecraft, NASA's Orion capsule, in Earth's orbit next year for Artemis III, a docking test mission before NASA's planned moon landing missions begin with Artemis IV.

data.title: South Korea says Nvidia will keep GPU pledges after Huang's resignation
data.description: SEOUL, Nov 13 : South Korea's Science and ICT Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said on Friday that Nvidia had confirmed it would go ahead with its previously announced pledge to supply 260,000 advanced graphics processing units (GPUs) to South Korea.  The commitment stands despite the resignation of Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, Bae said in a post on X.  The 260,000-GPU agreement was reached last year at Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings when Huang visited South Korea. Bae said Nvidia and South Korea would also continue to work on several joint projects, including linking Korean-made AI chips with Nvidia's platform, building AI computing infrastructure and joint research and talent development in physical AI.

data.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, letting AI agents pay for purchases
data.description: Nov 13 : OpenAI said on Friday it has launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets AI agents pay for purchases without accessing users' card details, with a security check required for every transaction. Here are more details: • The wallet has been built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, OpenAI said • It will initially be available in the US to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards. It can be accessed through "dots", the company's always-on AI agents • Users can review items, the total and the selected card before each purchase, then approve it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan • The payment network will provide a payment token in place of the actual card details, so neither the business nor the agent can see them, the company said • OpenAI expects users to eventually delegate purchases to agents within certain set parameters, such as spending limits, categories or time periods

data.title: Cerebras shares surge as forecast raise, surprise profit ease AI spending worries
data.description: Nov 13 : Cerebras Systems' shares gained more than 14 per cent in early trading on Friday, after the chipmaker raised its annual sales forecast and posted a surprise profit, indicating momentum in its challenge to Nvidia in the AI chip market. The gains, if they hold, would add over $3 billion to Cerebras' market value, as the upbeat forecast helped offset concerns over heavy AI spending and the uncertainty triggered by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. • As of Thursday's close, Cerebras' shares were down 47.2 per cent from their May IPO price of $185 apiece • Cerebras now expects 2026 adjusted revenue of $940 million to $960 million, up from its previous forecast of $880 million to $890 million • Analysts, on average, expected sales of $887.04 million for the period, according to data compiled by LSEG • The chipmaker reiterated plans to triple revenue in 2027, and said it has signed a cloud deal with Microsoft, with details to be shared next year • On the earnings call, CEO Andrew Feldman said delivery delays under Cerebras' $20 billion multi-year OpenAI deal stemmed from industry-wide shortages of land and power, rather than chip manufacturing constraints • Its adjusted cloud and services revenue, which reflects the OpenAI deal, more than tripled to $144.9 million for the third quarter • Adjusted profit came in at $29.82 million, compared with an adjusted loss of $10.86 million a year earlier. Analysts were expecting an adjusted loss of $38.4 million

data.title: China warns against new export controls on US chips after Nvidia scandal
data.description: BEIJING: China warned the United States on Friday (Nov 13) against putting additional export controls on semiconductors in the wake of the scandal surrounding AI chip giant Nvidia. China "has consistently opposed the abuse of export control measures, which disrupts the stability of global industrial and supply chains and serves no party's interests," foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular briefing when asked about calls from US lawmakers to impose more limits on exports of chip equipment to China. "China and the United States should work together to implement the important consensus reached by their respective heads of state and maintain the stable development of China-US economic and trade relations," Mao said. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang - who resigned on Thursday - has admitted to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang , a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed . Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China. US media quoted US lawmakers as saying that they were in favour of imposing additional export controls on chips to China as a result of the snowballing scandal. "The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here. I'm in favour of limiting those exports," House speaker Mike Johnson was quoted as saying. "I think there is a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take." US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging that Alice Huang - no relation to Jensen Huang - was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations and on Thursday said that they are a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" to stop China advancing in artificial intelligence technology. The furore comes ahead of a meeting expected next week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Shenzhen in southern China at an APEC gathering.

data.title: Quantum Systems says grounded German military drones flying again after cyberattack
data.description: BERLIN, Nov 13 : German defence technology group Quantum Systems said drones in service with the German military were flying again after they were grounded as a precaution following a cyberattack last month. The Financial Times reported on Thursday that the Bundeswehr had grounded drones made by Quantum Systems after the attack. "The fleet is operating normally around the globe — including Germany and the Bundeswehr," a Quantum Systems spokesperson said in an emailed statement. "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution." The Financial Times said the grounding had prevented Quantum Systems from taking part in a recent exercise with the military. There was no immediate comment from the German military. Quantum said "an active cyberattack by hostile actors" was detected in October but was contained by its IT and cybersecurity teams "in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities". "Through the quick measures taken and the characteristics of the incident, there is no risk in operating Quantum Systems' unmanned systems for the end users and the operators," it said. It was not immediately clear whether other companies may have been affected by the attack. Quantum Systems signed a deal last month to supply Ukraine with jet interceptors.

data.title: Tabletop games' popularity holds up as people seek off-screen connections, Asmodee CEO says
data.description: Nov 13 : Demand for tabletop games is holding strong as people seek ways to play together in person, Asmodee CEO Thomas Koegler told Reuters ahead of the busy end-of-year shopping season. Sweden-based Asmodee owns the rights to many globally known board games such as Catan and Carcassonne. It also distributes other publishers' titles, including Pokémon, Hasbro's Magic: The Gathering and Bandai Namco's One Piece trading card games. "What's clear is that our industry benefits from very strong sociological dynamics of spending time with your loved ones," Koegler said in an interview on Friday. He expects game nights to remain a popular Saturday plan, especially over Christmas, when darker weather makes games more appealing. The end-of-year holidays are a key sales season for game and toy companies. Board games have gained popularity among 16- to 25-year-olds, who are now putting them "at the heart" of their social life, Koegler said. An international barometer compiled by Asmodee and Kantar in 2026 showed that 74 per cent of the so-called "Gen Z" thought that in-person experiences were more important than digital ones. Koegler also pointed to rising attendance at trade events such as Spiel Essen and Gen Con, and hobby stores engaging local player communities, as two indicators that Asmodee's efforts to engage players through in-person events were working. "We see increasing of sales (in hobby stores), which means an increase in sell-out from them, because they are this nexus of local communities," Koegler said. ORGANIZED PLAY SUPPORTS TRADING CARD GAMES Organized play also holds a strong place in the success of trading card games, a category that Koegler has previously described as extremely strong and lasting. "All the events are packed because people really engage," he said. The Netherlands' largest board game event Spellenspektakel, which also hosts Europe's biggest trading card game event CardCon, reported 33,000 visitors at its 2026 edition on November 7-8, with a sold-out first day. Asmodee's sales grew 18.4 per cent in the board game category and 51.6 per cent in trading card games during its most recent quarter that ended in September. Hasbro's earnings were also boosted by its flagship trading card game "Magic: The Gathering" ahead of the holiday season.

data.title: Japan core inflation seen above BOJ target for second month in October: Reuters poll
data.description: TOKYO, Nov 13 : Japan's core consumer inflation is expected to surpass the central bank's 2 per cent target for the second straight month in October as the impact from the US-Israeli war on Iran continues, a Reuters poll showed on Friday.     • The nationwide core consumer price index, which includes energy items but excludes fresh food prices, is expected to have grown 2.3 per cent in October from a year earlier, according to a poll of 16 economists • That compared with a 2.1 per cent gain in September and put core inflation above the Bank of Japan's 2 per cent target — the strongest since last December. • "We expect to see continued strong inflation for food products excluding rice, as well as daily necessities due to the situation in Iran," said Ryosuke Katagi, a market economist at Mizuho Securities • Data from the Bank of Japan on Thursday showed the nation's wholesale inflation re-accelerated in October as the Middle East conflict and AI-related demand kept pushing up prices for fuel and semiconductor chips. • The BOJ held interest rates steady in October, but declared victory in hitting its price target. The central bank must focus on anchoring it around that level, it said • The internal affairs ministry will release CPI data at 8:30 a.m. on Friday, November 20 (2330 GMT on November 19)
